title: hnA TacFPS Aim Guide
author: trgjtk
scope: TacFPS practice for Valorant and other low-time-to-kill games. Aim training develops the mouse-control component and must be paired with in-game deathmatch or an equivalent transfer activity.
concepts: Transfer depends on practising the mouse movement the game demands, not merely raising an aim-trainer score.
A flick combines the path toward the target with the ability to decelerate and stop on it. Fast TacFPS acquisition puts unusual emphasis on stopping power.
Misses tend to extend along the direction of travel: at higher speed, overshoot and undershoot grow more than sideways path error.
Large static targets permit speed without enough precision; tiny static targets often reward accuracy at a slower speed. Training should deliberately cover both ends and the transition between them.
Horizontal and vertical acquisition impose different joint and lever demands, so both need exposure rather than assuming one transfers perfectly to the other.
practice_rules: Follow the execution goal for the current routine; the same scenario produces a different adaptation when played for raw speed versus clean pathing.
Pair the routines with game-specific deathmatch so mouse control is integrated with movement, crosshair placement, target recognition, and decisions.
Rotate the three routines one per day. Use Speed and Stopping more often when fast acquisition is the main limitation; use Smooth Pathing more often when lines and corrections are uncontrolled.
Treat discomfort as a stop signal. Productive speed work may involve brief controlled tension, but pain and sustained gripping are not training goals.
rotation: Default cycle: Speed and Stopping, Speed-to-Precision, Smooth Pathing. When uncertain, repeat that three-day cycle. A speed-biased cycle can repeat the first routine before continuing to the second and third.

routines.name: hnA TacFPS Routine - Speed and Stopping
routines.variant: hnA TacFPS Routine - Speed and Stopping
routines.description: Raw acquisition speed and controlled deceleration. Hold Mouse1 continuously, snap aggressively, and reacquire immediately after a miss rather than polishing the path.
routines.sensitivity: Use normal in-game sensitivity; the source assumes roughly 35-70 cm/360.
author_guidance: Hold Mouse1 continuously for every scenario in this routine.
Snap onto each target as fast as physically possible; large misses are acceptable while training this speed.
Reacquire immediately after a miss. Both the initial flick and the correction should be fast, and the correction does not need to be one clean movement.
Do not optimize for smoothness in this routine. The intended adaptation is raw acquisition speed and stopping power.
Use the target-switching and static exercises together to practise rapid acquisition across different movement sizes and directions.

exercises.focus: Use horizontal short, medium, and long switches to practise rapid stops.

performance_guide.setup: Use normal in-game sensitivity (the source assumes about 35-70 cm/360) and hold Mouse1 continuously.
steps: Snap to every target as fast as physically possible.
Use the full mix of short, medium, and long horizontal switches.
When you miss, reacquire immediately with another fast movement; the correction does not need to be clean.
performance_guide.success: Acquisition and stopping are maximally aggressive. Large misses and rough corrections are acceptable; smoothness and score are not the objective.

exercises.focus: Accelerate and stop over the smaller movements common after sound crosshair placement.

performance_guide.setup: Use normal in-game sensitivity and hold Mouse1 continuously.
steps: Attack each small-FOV switch with immediate acceleration.
Stop rapidly on the target despite the short travel distance.
Reacquire at full speed after a miss instead of slowing down to clean the path.
performance_guide.success: Short flicks feel forceful and decisive. Missing is acceptable when you are genuinely pushing acceleration and stopping speed.

exercises.focus: Keep the same aggressive acquisition while handling more vertical displacement.

performance_guide.setup: Use normal in-game sensitivity and hold Mouse1 continuously.
steps: Snap as fast as possible rather than tracking smoothly between targets.
Preserve the same aggression on vertical and diagonal switches.
Correct misses immediately and quickly, even if more than one correction is needed.
performance_guide.success: Vertical displacement does not make you hesitate or deliberately smooth the movement.

exercises.focus: Snap quickly, then stabilize on the small target.

performance_guide.setup: Use normal in-game sensitivity and hold Mouse1 continuously.
steps: Drive the initial movement toward the target at maximum speed.
Decelerate and stabilize contact on the smaller static target.
If contact is lost, reacquire immediately rather than restarting slowly.
performance_guide.success: You combine the speed routine's aggressive initial snap with enough stopping power to stabilize on target; a polished path is not required.

exercises.scenario: Pokeball Frenzy Auto Wide Wall 3 Targets
exercises.focus: Apply fast stops across wider target spacing.

performance_guide.setup: Use normal in-game sensitivity and hold Mouse1 continuously.
steps: Accelerate hard across the wide target spacing.
Stop and stabilize on each smaller target.
Make every reacquisition fast; do not turn this into a smoothness run.
performance_guide.success: Wide switches remain aggressive while the endpoint becomes stable enough to maintain contact.

exercises.focus: Combine a forceful initial movement with precise stabilization.

performance_guide.setup: Use normal in-game sensitivity and hold Mouse1 continuously.
steps: Snap forcefully toward each extra-small target.
Use stopping power to stabilize without deliberately slowing the initial movement.
Reacquire a miss as fast as possible, even when the correction is imperfect.
performance_guide.success: The small target challenges the endpoint, but you retain the routine's raw-speed intent instead of chasing accuracy or score.

exercises.focus: Reacquire the blinking target immediately, like correcting onto an unexpected swing.

performance_guide.setup: Use normal in-game sensitivity and hold Mouse1 continuously.
steps: The instant the target blinks, snap back onto it as fast as possible.
Treat each displacement like correcting onto an opponent who swung away from your crosshair placement.
Prioritize immediate reacquisition over a smooth or single correction.
performance_guide.success: There is minimal delay between the blink and your correction, and you lock back onto the target aggressively.

routines.name: hnA TacFPS Routine - Speed-to-Precision
routines.description: Bridge raw speed into consistent static acquisition. Perform the speed runs first, then retain the initial pace while cleaning up the final correction during accuracy runs.
routines.sensitivity: The source recommends roughly 25-35 cm/360 for this block.
author_guidance: Use this routine to carry the speed from Routine 1 into more consistent and precise acquisition.
In fuglaaPressure, attempt every target before it disappears; missing matters less than making every attempt.
For the three static scenarios, always complete the prescribed speed runs before the accuracy runs.
During speed runs, increase shots fired while keeping accuracy between 60% and 80%.
During accuracy runs, target 90-95% accuracy while retaining the fast initial flick and making the final micro-correction disciplined.
For the reflex scenarios, use one motion to the target and one back to center; adjust time scale or difficulty using the stated accuracy thresholds.

exercises.focus: Attempt every target before it disappears. Use the four-target version when accuracy remains below 60%.

steps: Aim faster than feels comfortable for static targets.
Attempt every visible target before it disappears.
Do not pause or become conservative merely to avoid misses.
performance_guide.success: You attempt the full pressure sequence; making every attempt matters more than avoiding misses.
performance_guide.adjust: If accuracy is below 60%, use fuglaaPressure 4 bots until the six-bot version is manageable.

exercises.focus: Do 7 speed runs at 60-80% accuracy, then 3 disciplined accuracy runs at 90-95%.

performance_guide.setup: Use about 25-35 cm/360. Complete all speed runs before any accuracy runs.
steps: Runs 1-7: push shots fired and speed while holding 60-80% accuracy.
Runs 8-10: target 90-95% accuracy.
During accuracy runs, retain the fast initial flick, then discipline the final micro-correction onto target.
performance_guide.success: Speed runs stay below 80% but not below 60%; accuracy runs reach roughly 90-95% without making the initial flick passive.

exercises.focus: Do 5 speed runs at 60-80% accuracy, then 2 accuracy runs at 90-95%.

performance_guide.setup: Use about 25-35 cm/360. Complete all speed runs before any accuracy runs.
steps: Runs 1-5: increase shots fired while keeping accuracy between 60% and 80%.
Runs 6-7: target 90-95% accuracy.
Keep the initial flick fast in both phases; clean up the final micro-adjustment during the accuracy phase.
performance_guide.success: The phase change improves endpoint discipline without discarding the speed built in the first five runs.

exercises.focus: Do 3 speed runs at 60-80% accuracy, then 2 accuracy runs at 90-95%.

performance_guide.setup: Use about 25-35 cm/360. Complete all speed runs before any accuracy runs.
steps: Runs 1-3: push shots fired across the wide spacing while holding 60-80% accuracy.
Runs 4-5: target 90-95% accuracy.
Maintain the fast initial flick, then make the last micro-correction deliberate enough to land.
performance_guide.success: You carry stopping power across wide movements, then convert it into 90-95% endpoint accuracy in the final two runs.

exercises.focus: Use one movement out and back. Increase time scale above 50% accuracy; reduce it below 25%.

performance_guide.setup: Use about 25-35 cm/360 and keep the scenario difficult enough to demand a reflexive response.
steps: Use one decisive motion from center to the target.
Use one decisive motion back to center.
Avoid adding several corrective movements to rescue the attempt.
performance_guide.success: Accuracy sits in the challenging 25-50% range while the out-and-back actions remain single movements.
performance_guide.adjust: Above 50% accuracy, increase time scale. Below 25%, reduce time scale.

exercises.focus: Use one decisive movement to the target and one back to center; switch to an easier version below 25% accuracy.

performance_guide.setup: Use about 25-35 cm/360 and begin with the Hard version.
steps: Use one decisive motion from center to the target.
Use one decisive motion back to center.
Do not turn the attempt into repeated corrections.
performance_guide.success: Accuracy remains challenging while each direction is completed as one motion.
performance_guide.adjust: Above 50% accuracy, increase difficulty or speed. Below 25%, use an easier Reflex Flick version.

routines.name: hnA TacFPS Routine - Smooth Pathing
routines.description: Train the opposite end of the spectrum: direct lines, minimal correction, and clean stops. Slow down enough to make the path deliberate rather than chasing score.
routines.sensitivity: The source recommends roughly 20-25 cm/360 for this block.
author_guidance: This routine deliberately trains the smoothness and pathing end of the spectrum rather than raw speed.
For the static and pokeball exercises, use the straightest possible path, minimize micro-corrections, and stop cleanly on target.
Move slowly enough to preserve that efficient path; score and maximum pace are not the objective here.
For the two tracking exercises, follow the slow target precisely without shaking off it.
Use the tracking work to clean up flick paths and final micro-adjustments.

exercises.focus: Draw straight paths and stop cleanly with as few micro-corrections as possible.

performance_guide.setup: Use about 20-25 cm/360 and deliberately reduce pace.
steps: Move along the straightest practical line to each target.
Use as few micro-corrections as possible.
Finish with a clean stop directly on target rather than rushing the shot.
performance_guide.success: Paths are efficient and stops are clean, even though the crosshair must move slowly. Score and maximum pace are not objectives.

exercises.focus: Prioritize line efficiency and deliberate stops over pace.

performance_guide.setup: Use about 20-25 cm/360 and slow down enough to control the path.
steps: Draw the straightest practical target-to-target line.
Avoid unnecessary micro-corrections near the extra-small target.
Stop cleanly on target before continuing.
performance_guide.success: The small targets do not make the path curve or produce repeated endpoint corrections; pace remains secondary.

exercises.focus: Keep long movements straight and settle without extra correction.

performance_guide.setup: Use about 20-25 cm/360 and deliberately reduce pace.
steps: Keep each long movement as straight and efficient as possible.
Minimize endpoint micro-corrections.
Settle with a clean stop on the target before moving again.
performance_guide.success: Wide movements stay direct instead of arcing, and the endpoint does not require repeated cleanup.

exercises.focus: Maintain a clean line into stable contact on each target.

performance_guide.setup: Use about 20-25 cm/360 and move slowly enough to preserve path quality.
steps: Approach every target on the straightest practical line.
Make stable contact without shaking or curving into the target.
Reduce micro-corrections and finish each acquisition with a clean stop.
performance_guide.success: Contact is stable and the route into each target is visibly efficient; speed and score remain secondary.

exercises.focus: Track the slow target without visible shake to clean up pathing and final corrections.

performance_guide.setup: Use about 20-25 cm/360 and a relaxed grip that permits smooth pursuit.
steps: Follow the slow target precisely rather than predicting ahead of it.
Keep the crosshair on target without shaking off.
Correct drift gently instead of snapping back and forth.
performance_guide.success: Contact remains smooth and stable with minimal visible jitter, supporting cleaner flick paths and micro-adjustments.

exercises.focus: Use precise smooth pursuit without introducing corrective jitter.

performance_guide.setup: Use about 20-25 cm/360 and a relaxed grip that permits continuous smooth movement.
steps: Track the slow target precisely through its path.
Avoid shaking off target or repeatedly correcting around it.
Let the pursuit movement stay continuous and controlled.
performance_guide.success: The crosshair remains steadily attached to the target with minimal jitter, reinforcing clean pathing and micro-adjustments.
